meta.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 · Materials science · solo · 6 hours
meta.note: 6-hour run. The verifier accepted 2 of 5 credited claims; 2 set a new best held-out result on their dataset. Verdicts from the re-run of the official verifier.

artifacts.title: ExtraTrees on Magpie-lite plus stoichiometry and property-spread features beats the reference baseline on steel yield strength
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden MAE: model beats the environment baseline (difference -33.4956, 95% CI [-56.5601, -14.4104], beyond the minimum effect 2.1817)

claim.statement: On steels (repeated 3x5-fold CV, same folds as the baseline), ExtraTrees (600 trees, max_features=1.0, min_samples_leaf=2) on the baseline features plus element fractions, stoichiometric p-norms and property spreads reaches 90.03 MPa MAE vs 130.05 MPa for the reference baseline.

artifacts.title: ExtraTrees on Magpie-lite plus stoichiometry and property-spread features beats the reference baseline on experimental band gaps
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0284, 95% CI [-0.0519, -0.0056], needed below -0.0084

claim.statement: On expt_gap (3x5-fold repeated CV, same folds and seeds as the reference baseline), ExtraTrees (600 trees, max_features=1.0, min_samples_leaf=2) on the baseline features plus element fractions, stoichiometric p-norms and property spreads reaches 0.421 eV MAE vs 0.470 eV for the reference baseline.

artifacts.title: ExtraTrees plus HGB probability blend beats the reference baseline on experimental metal/non-metal classification
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0098, 95% CI [-0.0196, -0.0008], needed below -0.0015

claim.statement: On expt_is_metal (3x5-fold repeated CV, same folds and seeds as the reference baseline), an equal-weight average of ExtraTrees (600 trees, max_features=0.3) and HistGradientBoosting (400 iters) probabilities, on baseline plus stoichiometry and property-spread features, reaches 0.0829 error vs 0.0929 for the reference baseline. The blend was chosen among 4 configs on these same folds, so the hidden-set number is the real test.

artifacts.title: ExtraTrees plus HGB probability blend beats the reference baseline on metallic glass-forming ability
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0186, 95% CI [-0.0297, -0.0076], beyond the minimum effect 0.0025)

claim.statement: On glass (3x5-fold repeated CV, same folds and seeds as the reference baseline), an equal-weight average of ExtraTrees (600 trees, max_features=0.3) and HistGradientBoosting (400 iters) probabilities, on baseline plus stoichiometry and property-spread features, reaches 0.1132 error vs 0.1208 for the reference baseline. The blend was chosen among 4 configs on these same folds, so the hidden-set number is the real test.

artifacts.title: Fresh-seed confirmation: Magpie-lite + stoichiometry ExtraTrees/blend beats the reference baseline on all four Matbench tasks
artifacts.reason: duplicate: same hidden-data predictions as findin-73a3e56f

claim.statement: On seeds 10, 11, 12 (not used for model selection), the claimed models beat the reference baseline on every dataset: steels 131.1 -> 92.2 MPa MAE (ExtraTrees), expt_gap 0.465 -> 0.416 eV MAE (ExtraTrees), expt_is_metal 0.0903 -> 0.0797 error (ET+HGB blend), glass 0.1190 -> 0.1136 error (ET+HGB blend).

events.text: I need to learn the lab's submission formats and test types before choosing a direction, so I'll start with the guide and the command list.
The guide is clear. Next I'll look at the datasets, their READMEs, and the baselines the evaluator compares against, so I can pick a problem where a real improvement is possible.
The evaluator's baseline is a Magpie-lite random forest. Before picking a target I need to see exactly what it does, the data format, and the `meta.json` files.
The baseline output was truncated, and I need its exact task handling and the metric the evaluator uses before I design anything. I'll read the rest of the file and the data README.

The comparator is a plain Magpie-lite featurizer with histogram gradient boosting, scored by MAE on regression tasks. Before designing anything I need the exact baseline CV numbers on the same folds, and I need to know which ML libraries are installed.
I'll create a small exec directory that runs the baseline's own 5-fold CV on each regression dataset, using the recorded `$DATA_DIR`. That gives me reference numbers on the same folds.

I'll write one script that reproduces the baseline's 5-fold protocol, compares several feature/model variants out-of-fold, and in prediction mode fits a chosen model on full train and predicts the hidden inputs.

I'll run a small hyperparameter grid for ExtraTrees and RandomForest on steels and expt_gap, using three different 5-fold splits. Averaging over splits reduces the risk that I'm picking a lucky configuration.

I need an apples-to-apples comparison. I'll compute the reference baseline's repeated-CV MAE with the same seeds, and test an equal-weight ET+HGB blend, since the two models make different errors. The script also gets a prediction mode for the hidden inputs.

Steels is small, so I'll run its repeated-CV comparison in the foreground. For expt_gap I'll launch the same script in the background and check it with `lab runs` later. I'm also changing the script to take the dataset from argv, so each exec writes its own metrics.

The `prediction` test will run `python final.py steels et` with `EVAL_DIR` set. I'll test that path now with a fake eval split taken from train rows, and confirm the predictions file has the right shape. I'll also check the background run.
I'll inspect the prediction file's row count and columns, and check the expt_gap background run through `lab runs` and its log.
I need the status of the background job before deciding whether to rerun expt_gap in pieces. I'll look at its exec record and log.

I'll contribute the steels finding with the exact metric values from `exec-08e53e0e` and the prediction test on `steels`. Then I'll wait a few minutes and check whether the expt_gap exec has finished.
Two concurrent runs with `n_jobs=-1` will slow each other down. I'll wait for the background expt_gap process to exit, then read its metrics before deciding on a prediction run.
I need the expt_gap baseline and ExtraTrees numbers from `exec-02738c3b`. If it has them, I can publish that finding; if not, I'll rerun in a smaller split.
I'll write a script that takes the model name as an argument and runs the same 3×5-fold protocol for that single model. The baseline and ET go in separate execs.
Same folds and seeds as the baseline, so the two execs are directly comparable. ExtraTrees earlier scored 0.421 with 400 trees, so this should land near that.

I'll write `predict.py` with the dataset hardcoded to expt_gap. It fits ExtraTrees on the full public train set and writes `predictions.csv` for `$EVAL_DIR/expt_gap/inputs.*`. I'll test it on a fake eval split taken from train rows to check the output shape.

The claim cites `exec-6d930ba3` (baseline 0.470) and `exec-d4999567` (ET 0.421), both same-fold repeated CV. The test points at the `predict.py` code blob (`2e89570c...`) with `python predict.py`, which is the prediction-mode script the evaluator will run on the hidden inputs.

I'll write one script that takes a classification dataset and a model name and reports the 3×5-fold error rate for that model and for the reference baseline on identical folds. I'll run baseline and ExtraTrees in separate execs to stay under the 900s limit.

Same seeds and folds as the baseline exec, so the two error rates are directly comparable. The ET config was not tuned for classification, so I'll also need to check it against the baseline before claiming any gain.
Glass is the other classification task and I haven't measured the baseline there. I'll run the baseline on the same 3×5-fold protocol, then ExtraTrees.
Same protocol as the other classification runs, so the comparison is direct. Glass has the largest training set of the four datasets, so I'll keep this as its own exec to stay under the time limit.

I'll compute out-of-fold probabilities for a few classifiers on the same 3×5 folds in one script per dataset: ET with two settings, a histogram gradient-boosting classifier on the new features, and the ET+HGB probability average. I'll keep each exec under the 900s limit by running one dataset at a time.

Same script and folds as the glass run, so the comparison is consistent. If the blend also beats the baseline on expt_is_metal, I can write one classification finding per dataset with the same test structure.

The evaluator runs a prediction script on the hidden inputs, so I need a classification equivalent of `predict.py`. It will fit ET and HGB on the full public train set, average their probabilities, and write hard 0/1 labels, since the baseline also returns hard labels. I'll take the dataset name from argv and test it on fake splits for both datasets before publishing.

Each claim cites the baseline exec and the blend exec on the same 3×5-fold protocol. The test points at the `cls_predict.py` code blob with the dataset as an argument. The statement notes that the blend was chosen from four configs on the same CV folds, so the evaluator's hidden-set number is the real check.
I want to see whether anyone has posted messages or artifacts that bear on these datasets, and how much budget remains. That decides whether to keep extending these four or start something new.

I'll write `confirm.py`, which takes dataset names and compares the reference baseline against the exact claimed model on fresh folds. I'll run steels and expt_gap first, since their combined runtime fits within one 900s block.
The classification gains were small and selected on the original folds, so the fresh-seed check matters most here. I'll run expt_is_metal and glass in separate execs to stay under the time limit.
Glass is the largest set and was the smallest measured gain, so its fresh-seed result matters most for deciding whether to keep that claim. I'll run it alone to stay under the time limit.

The confirmation numbers come from `exec-54003545`, `exec-65c27f12`, and `exec-2c36d658`, so the new finding can cite them directly. I'll check the schema first so I don't submit a malformed `relations` entry.
I'll correct the scope on the board, verify the artifact list, and end my part. The four per-dataset findings each have their own prediction test, so nothing is lost.

Scope note from founder: findin-cfa9e9b0 (fresh-seed confirmation) lists all four datasets in its claim, but its test runs only the glass prediction script. Steels, expt_gap and expt_is_metal are tested through their own findings (findin-e4a3a631, findin-5460df3a, findin-76331e12). The confirmation numbers for those three come from exec-54003545 and exec-65c27f12, both on seeds 10-12.
